1.2.1.v: All affixes after the verb गाङ् 'to study' and the verb कुट् 'to be crooked' and the rest, are as if they had an indicatory ङ् (ङित्), except those affixes which have an indicatory ञ् (ञित्) or ण् (णित्).
1.2.1.e: The non-ञित् and non-णित्  प्रत्ययाः attached to the - (1) the 'गाङ्' आदेश (that happens to the धातु 'इङ् अध्ययने'), and (2) the verbs of the कुटादिगण (an अन्तर्गण of तुदादिगण) - behave as if they are ङित्.

1.2.2.v: An affix which begins with the augment इट् -- आर्धधातुकस्येड् वलादेः [[7.2.35]], is ङित् after the root विज् 'to fear, to move'.
1.2.2.e: A प्रत्यय that gets an इडागम is considered ङित् when attached to the dhatu 'विज्'.

1.2.3.v: After the verb ऊर्ण 'to cover', the affix beginning with the augment इट् is regarded optionally like ङित्।

1.2.4.v: A सार्वधातुक -- तिङ्शित्सार्वधातुकम् [[3.4.113]], affix not having an indicatory ङित्।
1.2.4.e: An अपित् सार्वधातुकप्रत्ययः behaves like a ङित् प्रत्यय.
1.2.4.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.2.5.v: The affixes of लिट् (Perfect Tense) not coming after a conjunct consonant, are as if they had an indicatory क् (कित्).
1.2.5.e: For a verb root that does not end in a संयोग, the अपित् प्रत्यय of  लिट्-लकार behaves like a कित् प्रत्यय.
1.2.5.sa: संयोगभिन्नवर्णात्  परस्य लिट्-लकारस्य अपित् प्रत्ययः कित्वत् भवति ।
1.2.5.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.2.6.v: The लिट् (Perfect Tense) affixes after the roots इन्धि 'to kindle' and भू 'to become' are also कित्।

1.2.7.v: The affix क्त्वा is कित् after मृड् 'to be gracious', मृद् 'to squeeze', गुध् 'to wrap up', कुष् 'to tear', क्लिश् 'to suffer', वद् 'to speak' and वस् 'to dwell'.

1.2.8.v: The affixes क्त्वा and सन् [[3.1.7]] are कित् after रुद् 'to weep', विद् 'to know', मुष् 'to steal', गृह् 'to seize', स्वप् 'to sleep' and प्रच्छ् 'to ask'.

1.2.9.v: The affix सन् beginning with a letter of the प्रत्यहार झल् is like कित् after the verbs ending in इक् vowels.

1.2.10.v: And after a root ending in a consonant and preceded by a vowel of the प्रत्यहार इक् , the affix सन् beginning with a झल् consonant, is like कित् ।

1.2.11.v: After roots ending in a consonant, that adjoins a vowel of इक् प्रत्यहार , the substitutes of the -- विधिनिमन्त्रणामन्त्रण अधीष्टसम्प्रश्नप्रार्थनेषु लिङ् [[3.3.161]] and सिच् -- च्लेः सिच् [[3.1.44]], when they begin with a consonant of झल् प्रत्यहार , are कित् when the आत्मनेपद affixes follow.

1.2.12.v: And after the verbs ending in ऋ , the substitutes of लिङ् and the affix सिच् , are कित् , when they begin with झल् and the आत्मनेपद affixes follow.

1.2.13.v: Optionally after the verb गम् , the लिङ् and the सिच् beginning with झल् consonants, in the आत्मनेपद , are कित्।

1.2.14.v: The सिच् आत्मनेपद affixes are कित् after the root हन् 'to kill'.

1.2.15.v: The affix सिच् before आत्मनेपद affixes is कित् after the verb यम् when meaning 'to divulge'.

1.2.16.v: The affix सिच् before आत्मनेपद affixes is कित् optionally when यम् means 'to expose'.

1.2.17.v: The affix सिच् before आत्मनेपद affixes is कित् after स्था 'to stand' and घु मृषस्तितिक्षायाम् [[1.2.20]] verbs, and these verbs change their आ into इ before these terminations.

1.2.18.v: The affix क्त्वा when it takes the augment इट् (i.e. when it is सेट्) is not कित् ।

1.2.19.v: The सेट् निष्ठा affixes are not कित् after the verbs शीङ् 'to lie down', स्विद् 'to sweat', मिद् 'to melt', क्ष्विद् 'to be unctuous', and दृश् 'to offend'.

1.2.20.v: The सेट् निष्ठा affix is not कित् after the verb मृष् 'to forbear'.

1.2.21.v: The सेट् निष्ठा affix is optionally not कित् after the verbs with a penultimate उ if used impersonally or denoting the beginning of action.

1.2.22.v: The सेट् निष्ठा affix and the सेट् क्त्वा are not कित् after the verb पुङ् 'to purify'.

1.2.23.v: The सेट् क्त्वा is optionally कित् after the verbs having a penultimate न् ending in a थ् and फ्।

1.2.24.v: The सेट् क्त्वा is optionally कित् after the verbs वञ्च् 'to cheat', लुञ्च् 'to pluck' and ऋत् 'to dare or abhor'.

1.2.25.v: The सेट् क्त्वा is optionally कित् , according to the opinion of ऋषि काश्यप after the verbs तृष् 'to be thirsty', मृष् 'to sprinkle' and कृश् 'to become lean'.

1.2.26.v: After a verb which begins in a consonant and ends in a letter of रल् प्रत्यहार and has as its penultimate इ or ई and उ or ऊ , the क्त्वा and सन् affixes are optionally कित् ।

1.2.27.v: A vowel whose time is that of short उ , ऊ and the prolated ऊ , is called respectively ह्रस्व short, दीर्घ long and प्लुत prolated.
1.2.27.e: Vowels are classified as ह्रस्व, दीर्घ and प्लुत based on the time taken for their pronunciation, as compared against the time of उ, ऊ and उ3 respectively.
1.2.27.sa: उ-ऊ-उ3 एतेषां उच्चारणकालः यस्य उच्चारणकालेन सह समानः, सः अच् क्रमेण ह्रस्वसंज्ञकः, दीर्घसंज्ञकः, प्लुतसंज्ञकः भवति ।
1.2.27.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.2.28.v: The short, long and prolated, when enunciated as such, by using these terms, are to be understood to come in the place of vowels only.
1.2.28.e: Action denoted by the words ह्रस्व / दीर्घ / प्लुत happens in place of an अच् letter.
1.2.28.sa: ह्रस्व-दीर्घ-प्लुत-शब्देन विधीयमानम् कार्यम् अच्-वर्णस्य स्थाने एव भवति ।
1.2.28.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.2.29.v: The vowel that is perceived as having a high tone is called उदात्त or acutely accented.
1.2.29.e: A vowel that is pronounced using the upper-half portion of its उच्चारणस्थान is known as उदात्त.
1.2.29.sa: यस्य स्वरस्य उच्चारणम् तस्य उच्चारणस्थानस्य ऊर्ध्वभागात् भवति, तस्य 'उदात्तः' इति संज्ञा भवति ।
1.2.29.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.2.30.v: The vowel that is perceived as having a low tone is called अनुदात्तः or gravely accented
1.2.30.e: A vowel that is pronounced using the lower-half portion of its उच्चारणस्थान is known as अनुदात्त.
1.2.30.sa: यस्य स्वरस्य उच्चारणम् तस्य उच्चारणस्थानस्य अधोभागात् भवति, तस्य 'अनुदात्तः' इति संज्ञा भवति ।
1.2.30.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.2.31.v: The vowel that has the combination of अनुदात्त and उदात्त tones is said to be स्वरित or circumflexly accented.
1.2.31.e: A vowel that is pronounced using the upper as well as lower portions of its उच्चारणस्थान is known as  स्वरित.
1.2.31.sa: यस्य स्वरस्य उच्चारणम् तस्य उच्चारणस्थानस्य उर्ध्वभागम् अधोभागम् च प्रयुज्य भवति,  तस्य 'स्वरित:' इति संज्ञा भवति ।
1.2.31.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.2.32.v: Of it (स्वरित-s) the first portion is उदात्त , to the extent of a half measure, or prosodial length.
1.2.32.e: The first half part of a स्वरित-स्वर is considered उदात्त.
1.2.32.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.2.33.v: In addressing a person from a distance the tone is called एकश्रुति or monotony.

1.2.34.v: In sacrificial works there is Monotony, except in जप (silent repetition of a formula), न्यूङ्ख vowels (16 sorts of ओम्) and the साम Vedas.

1.2.35.v: The pronunciation of the word वषट् , may optionally be by raising the voice (acutely accented), or it may be pronounced with monotony.

1.2.36.v: The monotony is optional in the recitation of the Vedas or they may be recited with accents.

1.2.37.v: There should be no Monotony in the recitation of the सब्रह्मण्य hymns and in those hymns, the vowels, that would otherwise have taken the स्वरित accent, take the उदात्त accent instead.

1.2.38.v: The words देवा and ब्राह्मण in those hymns have अनुदात्त accent.

1.2.39.v: The Monotony takes the place of the अनुदात्त vowels which follow the स्वरित vowels, in close proximity (संहिता).

1.2.40.v: The accent called सन्नतर is substituted in the room of an अनुदात्त vowel, which has an उदात्त or स्वरित vowel following it.

1.2.41.v: An affix consisting of a single letter is called अपृक्त।
1.2.41.e: A प्रत्ययः that contains only one letter is called अपृक्त ।
1.2.41.sa: यस्मिन् प्रत्यये केवलं एकः एव वर्णः अस्ति, अपृक्तः नाम्ना ज्ञायते ।
1.2.41.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.2.42.v: A तत्-पुरुष compound, the case of each member is the same, is called कर्मधारय or Appositional Determinative compound.

1.2.43.v: In (this book, in the sūtras relating to) compound, the word that is exhibited in the Nominative -1st case, is called उपसर्जन or the secondary word.

1.2.44.v: A word which is one fixed case, (while the word compounded with it may vary its case) is also उपसर्जन , except for the purposes of the the rule which requires the उपसर्जन to stand first in a compound.

1.2.45.v: A significant form of a word, not being a verbal root (धातु), or an affix (प्रत्यय) is called a प्रातिपदिक or crude-form.
1.2.45.e: A meaningful word which is not a धातु, not a प्रत्यय, and which does not end in  प्रत्यय is called a 'प्रातिपदिक'.
1.2.45.sa: यः अर्थवान् शब्दः धातुसंज्ञकः, प्रत्ययसंज्ञकः, प्रत्ययान्तः च नास्ति, तस्य 'प्रातिपदिकम्' इति संज्ञा भवति ।
1.2.45.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.2.46.v: The forms ending कृत् affixes or तद्धित affixes, or compound are also called प्रातिपदिक।
1.2.46.e: कृत्-प्रत्ययान्त words, तद्धितप्रत्ययान्त words and the सामासिकशब्दाः are known as प्रातिपदिक.
1.2.46.sa: कृत्-प्रत्ययान्तशब्दानाम्, तद्धितप्रत्ययान्तशब्दानाम् तथा सामासिकशब्दानाम् 'प्रातिपदिकम्' इति संज्ञा भवति ।
1.2.46.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.2.47.v: The short vowel is substituted in the neuter, for the final vowel, of a प्रातिपदिक।
1.2.47.e: The last letter of an अजन्त प्रातिपदिक is becomes हस्व in context of नपुंसकलिङ्ग.
1.2.47.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.2.48.v: A short vowel is the substitute of प्रातिपदिक which ends with the word गो 'a cow' and of that which ends with what has as its termination a feminine affix, when regarded as उपसर्जन।

1.2.49.v: When a तद्धित affix is elided by the word लुक् there takes place the elision by लुक् of feminine affix of the उपसर्जन।

1.2.50.v: The short is substituted in the place of गोणी , when the तद्धित affix is elided by लुक्।

1.2.51.v: When a तद्धित affix is elided by using the word लुप् , then the gender and number (of the derivative word) agree with those of the original word.

1.2.52.v: And of adjectives (the gender and number are the same as of the word formed by लुप् elision of the तद्धित and which they qualify) so far as the जाति (or kind of species) is concerned, (or when not expressing जाति).

1.2.53.v: This (concord or gender and number, of primitive and derivative nouns, and of attributes and substantives need not be taught (or approved), because it has the authority of संज्ञा (conventional term or idiom).

1.2.54.v: The sūtras declaring लुप् elision need not also be taught, because of the non-currency of the etymological meaning of the words supposed to be formed by लुप् elision.

1.2.55.v: And if the etymological meaning 'be held authoritative', then when such meaning is absent, the word also should vanish.

1.2.56.v: (Nor need be taught) the rule relating to the dependance of the meaning of a word on the principal (प्रधान in a compound) or on the affix (प्रत्यय) because the authority of the meaning (of a word, compound or derivative) consists in something else.

1.2.57.v: And a rule fixing the meaning of Tense (काल) and उपसर्जन (sequence) is equally (unnecessary, and need not be taught).

1.2.58.v: In (a common) name (expressive of) class, in denoting the singular, the plural is optionally used.

1.2.59.v: The plural of the pronoun अस्मद् 'I', is used optionally, though the sense requires a singular or a dual number.

1.2.60.v: And the dual of फाल्गुनी and प्रष्ठपदा , when signifying asterisms, (also connotes optionally plural).

1.2.61.v: In the Vedas, the two stars, पुनर्वासू , may optionally be singular, (and connote a dual).

1.2.62.v: In the Vedas, the two stars विशाखा may optionally be in the singular number.

1.2.63.v: In the द्वन्द compounds of the stars तिष्व and पुनर्वसू , the dual constantly comes in place of the plural.

1.2.64.v: Of the words having the same form and all in the same one case-termination, the last one is only retained.
1.2.64.e: If two or more words have identical forms for all विभक्तिs, then in usage only one word is used by applying appropriate वचन to it.
1.2.64.sa: सर्वासु विभक्तिषु येषां रूपाणि समानानि सन्ति, तेषु केवलं एकः शब्दः एव अवशिष्यते ।
1.2.64.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.2.65.v: The वृद्ध (or patronymic गोत्र word becomes एकशेष and is retained, when compounded) with a patronymic word युवन् , provided that the specific difference in form between them be in their signs (affix) only.

1.2.66.v: And so also a feminine word, ending with a वृद्ध affix, when similarly spoken along with the same word but which ends with a युवन् affix, is only retained and it is treated like a masculine.

1.2.67.v: A word in the masculine gender, similarly spoken along with the same word, but ending with the feminine affix, becomes एकशेष and the latter is dropped.

1.2.68.v: The words भ्रातृ 'brother' and पुत्र 'son', when spoken of along with स्वसृ 'sister' and दुहितृ 'daughter' respectively are only retained and the latter are dropped.

1.2.69.v: A neuter noun, which has the same form, only differing in affix, is optionally retained and the other is dropped and it is like a singular number.

1.2.70.v: The word पितृ 'father' is optionally only retained when spoken of along with मातृ 'mother'.

1.2.71.v: The word श्वशुर 'father-in-law', is optionally only retained, when spoken of along with श्वशुरू 'mother-in-law'.

1.2.72.v: The pronouns त्यद् etc. when spoken of along with any other noun, (pronoun other than त्यद् etc.) are always retained as एकशेष (to the exclusion of others).

1.2.73.v: The feminine noun is only retained when denoting a collection of domestic animals, not being young.
